correctness.rationale: The explicit coordinate change (X,-Y,alpha Z,-alpha W), alpha^4=-1, sends the maximal inner-Galois quartic X^4+XY^3+Z^4+ZW^3=0 to Schur's equation exactly. The Miura–Taki Proposition 3.3 eight points map to the four zeros on L: x0=x1=0 and four zeros on M: x2=x3=0 printed in Rojas–Lira Section 3. Because the Schur polynomial separates into quartics of disjoint coordinate pairs, each of the 4*4 joins P_iQ_j lies entirely on Schur; the 16 joins are distinct. Rojas–Lira Lemma 3.1 proves every Schur line meeting L or M is one of those sixteen; hence each of the eight points lies on precisely four lines and the 48 other lines avoid them. The global assertion that there are no *other* quadruple points uses the published full 64-line incidence census attributed to Nurowski, rather than the sixteen-line symbolic check. An accessible indexed technical summary of Nurowski explicitly states that the 64 lines have exactly eight quadruple points and sixteen distinguished join lines; the Nurowski full text could not be retrieved this run, so that literature-dependent global count was not independently enumerated; this is an explicit correctness residual dependence on a precise cited incidence theorem, not a fabricated independent 64-line verification.
